key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>20%, including lab abnormalities) include febrile neutropenia, diarrhea, mucositis, nausea, sepsis, neutropenia, headache. Serious adverse reaction in ≥5%: febrile neutropenia (11%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 10% of VANFLYTA patients, including sepsis (5%). QT prolongation was an important risk.

citations.quote: The most common (>20%) adverse reactions, including laboratory abnormalities, are lymphocytes decreased, potassium decreased, albumin decreased, phosphorus decreased, alkaline phosphatase increased, magnesium decreased, febrile neutropenia, diarrhea, mucositis, nausea, calcium decreased, abdominal pain, sepsis, neutropenia, headache, creatine phosphokinase increased, vomiting, and upper respiratory tract infection. (6.1)

Serious adverse reactions in \ge 5\% of patients who received VANFLYTA plus chemotherapy were: febrile neutropenia (11%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 10% of patients who received VANFLYTA plus chemotherapy, including sepsis (5%)

detail.text: WARNING: QT PROLONGATION, TORSADES DE POINTES, and CARDIAC ARREST. VANFLYTA prolongs the QT interval; torsades de pointes and cardiac arrest have occurred. Contraindicated in patients with severe hypokalemia, severe hypomagnesemia, or long QT syndrome. Do not initiate or escalate if QTcF > 450 ms. Available only through the VANFLYTA REMS.

citations.quote: ## WARNING: QT PROLONGATION, TORSADES DE POINTES, and CARDIAC ARREST

Torsades de pointes and cardiac arrest have occurred in patients receiving VANFLYTA. Do not administer VANFLYTA to patients with severe hypokalemia, severe hypomagnesemia, or long QT syndrome. (4, 5.1)
Do not initiate treatment with VANFLYTA or escalate the VANFLYTA dose if the QT interval corrected by Fridericia's formula (QTcF) is greater than 450 ms. (2.3, 5.1)

detail.text: VANFLYTA is available only through a restricted program called the VANFLYTA REMS, determined necessary to ensure the benefits outweigh the risks of QT prolongation, Torsades de Pointes, and cardiac arrest.

citations.quote: VANFLYTA is available only through a restricted program called the VANFLYTA Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS). (5.2)

In accordance with section 505-1 of FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for VANFLTYA (quizartinib) to ensure the benefits of the drug outweigh the risks of QT prolongation, Torsades de Pointes, and cardiac arrest.

detail.text: LeukoStrat CDx FLT3 Mutation Assay, an FDA-approved test for selection of AML patients with FLT3-ITD mutation for VANFLYTA treatment.

citations.quote: FLT3-ITD status was determined prospectively with a clinical trial assay and verified retrospectively using the companion diagnostic LeukoStrat® CDx FLT3 Mutation Assay, which is an FDA-approved test for selection of patients with AML for VANFLYTA treatment.

vote.text: No advisory committee was convened for this NDA; instead, two Special Government Employees (SGEs) were consulted on Feb 27 and March 6, 2023, and both concluded quizartinib has a favorable benefit-risk profile for use with induction and consolidation chemotherapy, while noting concerns about post-HSCT maintenance benefit.

summary.text: VANFLYTA (quizartinib) received regular approval under a Priority review for newly diagnosed FLT3-ITD positive AML, based on a statistically significant OS improvement in the pivotal QuANTUM-First trial. It had Fast-track designation (granted March 2022) and Orphan Drug Designation for AML (granted 2009). Approval carried a boxed warning for QT prolongation, Torsades de Pointes and cardiac arrest, and a REMS.
